decisions.rationale: Operator: 'we don't have to change the code's offset logic at all. this is purely a visualization build we will extend its capabilities later.' Future phase will revisit FK/offset migration when triggered (e.g. by gripper change).

decisions.decision: OBJ + MTL is the canonical mesh+color pipeline (NOT DAE, NOT URDF top-level materials)
decisions.rationale: Multi-visual URDF top-level material name lookup hits documented RViz2 bug (ros2/rviz#1293). DAE Lambert shading goes all-black on per-face flat normals. OBJ + Assimp's MTL auto-loading is per-mesh-group reliable. UR5e itself uses DAE, but UR's per-vertex normals are artist-authored differently than RG2's per-face USD authoring.

decisions.decision: Static TF rpy=(0, 0, π), xyz=(0, 0, 0) for tool0→rg2_base_link
decisions.rationale: Derived from live read of /World/UR5e/wrist_3_link and /World/RG2_Gripper world transforms after isaac-sim-mcp ur5e-dt quickstart physics-settle. Anchored on /World/RG2_Gripper (asset root), NOT the leaf onrobot_rg2_base_link prim — leaf has its own -90°-about-Z xformOp:orient that's already encoded in the URDF mesh visuals; double-counting it produces a clean 90° error.

context_notes: Phase 7 took several iterations to land the right approach. Initial DAE pipelines hit Lambert darkness + welding artifacts; STL + URDF top-level materials hit the multi-visual material bug; OBJ + MTL with USD-canonical color patching was the production answer. The journey produced reusable knowledge captured in ~/.claude/skills/isaac-sim-extension-dev/references/{usd-to-urdf-visualization.md,external-urdf-tf-attach.md} + 3 parameterized scripts (usd_to_obj_export.py, patch_obj_mtl_from_usd.py, derive_static_tf_from_isaacsim.py). The single biggest meta-lesson: when verifying mesh rendering quality, compare to Isaac Sim's render as ground truth (and use ask-gpt skill for visual diff) — Claude's own visual judgment is unreliable on subtle rendering differences. Also: TF arrows in RViz are red/green/blue and easy to mistake for mesh tints — disable TF visualization during color verification.
